title: docs(plugin-spec): use the page's own `@vendor/*` placeholder in the peerDependencies examples
body:
Fixes #18417

## What changed

Both `peerDependencies` examples on `content/docs/protocol/kernel/plugin-spec.mdx` pinned
`'@objectstack/ui': '^2.0.0'` — a package that is declared in neither this repo nor the npm
registry. Both sites now read `'@vendor/ui': '^2.0.0'`. The block stays, the range stays, the
two proposal-only disclaimers stay.

```diff
-    '@objectstack/ui': '^2.0.0',     (full manifest example)
+    '@vendor/ui': '^2.0.0',
-  '@objectstack/ui': '^2.0.0',       (Dependency Types, section 3 "Peer Dependencies")
+  '@vendor/ui': '^2.0.0',
```

Two lines, one file. Sites were located by content, not by line number.

## Why this arm (D), and why it invents nothing

Triage chose arm **D** — keep the block, move the name to the page's own placeholder form.
Reproduced independently on this branch, tree `objectstack-ai/objectstack` at
`84ba4a847600dbecb55fcd2e31322ada19496f58` (the branch base), file counts taken from the page
itself:

| reading | value |
| --- | --- |
| `@vendor/email` on the page | 2 — one of them in the **same code block**, on the sibling `optionalDependencies` key, five lines above the defect |
| `@vendor/analytics` on the page | 1 |
| any `package.json` in the repo declaring a `@vendor/*` name | **0** — so `@vendor/*` really is a placeholder family |
| firing control, same scan: `"name": "@objectstack/core"` | `packages/core/package.json` — the scan reaches |
| npm registry `@vendor/ui` | HTTP 404 |
| npm registry `@vendor/email` (the name the page already ships) | HTTP 404 — the new name is exactly as inert as the convention it joins |
| npm registry `@objectstack/core` (firing control) | HTTP 200 |

The page's other convention — `@objectstack/*` names a package that exists — was measured per
name rather than assumed: `core`, `spec`, `cli` each resolve to a real `packages/*/package.json`;
`ui` resolved to nothing, which is this card.

Arms B (name a real package) and C (delete the block) were both ruled out by triage, and A is the
defect itself. D is the only arm that satisfies both of the page's existing conventions at once.

## The one page convention that looked like a third one, and why it does not conflict

`@objectstack/testing` (3 occurrences, Plugin Testing section) is also declared nowhere and is
also 404 on npm — so the page does tolerate an inert `@objectstack/*` name in one place. It is not
a counter-example to D:

- its warn callout sits **five lines above its first use** and disclaims **the package**, verbatim:
  "there is no such published package today"; the two `peerDependencies` disclaimers disclaim **the
  manifest key** (the schema declares it) and say nothing about the package. Different subject;
  the precedent does not reach this site.
- following that precedent here would mean asserting on the page that an `@objectstack/ui` package
  is planned — inventing a fact, which is the objection that ruled out arm B.
- the page's own prose for this key reads "Use for large dependencies (React, Vue) that should be
  shared across plugins" — a third-party shared library, which is precisely what `@vendor/*` marks,
  and precisely what `@mycompany/*` (the reader's own org, 3 names on the page) does not.

No third convention conflicts with D, so this does not go back to triage.

## The follow-on delivery item triage proposed is NOT owed — reasoning

Triage suggested bringing the first example at line 71 inside the reach of the proposal-only
callout, on the premise that the nearest disclaimer is roughly 355 lines later. That premise does
not hold, twice over:

1. There are **two** proposal-only statements on this page, and the earlier one names
   `peerDependencies` explicitly ("The displayName / author / license / homepage /
   optionalDependencies / peerDependencies / metadata / config / marketplace keys above are
   proposal-only — the schema declares none of them"). It sits **112 lines after** the first
   example, not 355.
2. Stronger: the code block that **contains** the first example opens on its own first line with
   "src/manifest.ts — proposed authoring wrapper (see the callout below for the fields
   ManifestSchema actually declares today)". The pointer is already inside the block, above the
   defect.

A reader hitting line 71 is therefore inside a block that announces itself as a proposal and points
at the callout that grades it. Adding a third synonymous disclaimer to one page would be a new
defect, not a repair, so nothing further is added here.

## Verification

- `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived **39**
  families for this change set. All 39 were run; reconciliation with `--ran` reports
  `39 derived, 39 run, 0 UNRUN`.
- 34 were green on the first pass. Five refused as PREREQUISITE NOT MET against an unbuilt tree
  (`check:doc-formula-expressions`, `check:doc-security-posture`, `check:docs-transcript-drift` at
  exit 3; `check:docs` and `check:skill-examples` at exit 1 with prerequisite text). After building
  `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/lint...`, `@objectstack/formula` and `@objectstack/client-react...`,
  all five re-ran at exit 0. `check:skill-examples` is the one that actually reads this page's fenced
  TypeScript: "258 prose examples type-check across 3 surface(s)".
- Exit codes were captured before any pipe, per the gates' own instruction.
- Control-byte self-scan over the edited file: `grep -naP` for the control range returns exit 1, no
  matches.
- No ablation is offered: this diff adds no guard and changes no executable behaviour, so there is
  nothing whose failure could be demonstrated.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`, measured rather than assumed: of the 70 non-private workspace packages, **0**
carry a `files[]` entry matching content or docs; positive control on the same scan, **70** ship a
`dist` entry. Nothing published moves, so no released package takes a version bump from this diff.

## Acceptance notes

- `@objectstack/testing` is inert in the same way `@objectstack/ui` was, at 3 sites in the Plugin
  Testing section. It is already disclaimed in place by its own callout, and that section is held by
  the epic #15952, so it is left alone here — noted, not filed.
